tips.comment: Paradoxical has been in excellent form since December with a top 3 finish in 10 of the last 11 races including 6 wins. I also expect a win for Paradoxical today.
Has run well in 2 of his last 3 runs. Though it's more than 2 years since his last win, he ran his best race for ages last time. His turn could be near as he is well in on old form.

Odin Legacy made a strong start in handicaps when beaten just a length off 81 at Sandown, backing up his promising maiden form here. He didn’t handle soft ground on his final two runs of 2024, so getting back on the all-weather should suit him much better. Big shout if he picks up where he left off earlier in the year.

This looks the perfect race for Cavalry Call to get his head back in front was last seen at Kempton at the 1 mile trip where finishing a creditable 6th/13 steps up in trip here tackling the 1 mile 2 furlong trip for the first time that most certainly being a positive move by his connections as he has shown signs in past races that this trip is well worth exploring with this gelded son of Invincible Spirit currently operating on a mark of 73 it is very well possible he is a step ahead of the handicapper and is likely to have much bigger performance in the locker just waiting to be unleashed in very good time jockey Jack Mitchell takes the ride on Simon & Ed Crisford's inmate an can give him the perfect ride here at Chelmsford merits serious consideration

Curran’s form dipped after a decent third at Ayr last summer, but he’s had a wind operation since and returns off a much-reduced mark, now 13 lbs lower than his opening one. The drop back to 10f should suit better, and the yard has a good record with all-weather runners fresh (167 runs, 37 wins, 22% strike rate, +40 pts @ 24% ROI). If the operation has done the trick, he could go well at a nice price.

The favorite may take some beating, but in contrast, this horse seems to be racing off a competitive mark, whilst the favorite is nearing the top of its competitiveness. So, at the odds, it makes sense e/w.

Nice run on debut over 6f when third, running free and only beaten by 1 length at big odds. Can step forward here, dropping back to 5f, which is expected to suit best. Trainer has a good record on polytrack, being 49/18, 36% +73% ROI.

Walnut should improve on debut third, but Cape Sovereign has solid form on turf last year and sets the standard. Also, the switch to the all-weather can help, and has had a wind operation and been gelded. Can step forward.

Race 3 at Chelmsford City today is the Restricted Maiden Stakes (Class 5) for 3 to 5-year-olds over 1,006 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old filly Honest Courtesan from the Archie Watson yard, and she will be ridden by Hollie Doyle. This daughter of Kodiac is having her debut today and, on the face of it, has been placed well for her debut and is expected to be a major player here. Worth keeping an eye on.
Could nick the race from the front here. Close 2nd the last twice and comes here off the same mark, so has a big chance here.
3 times a winner over 6 furlongs here and a beaten favourite over that trip here last month. Yet to win over 5 furlongs in 7 attempts but has finished runner-up over course and distance.

Last outing can be ignored when 9/10 due to bad luck at the start with a poor draw and raced wide until he failed to get back inside at the first time of asking. His running stats suggest that 5f is his trip, and he runs off 60 once more. If he can get in position early, he has a really good chance here.

Sir Rodneyredblood can win Chelmsford’s 23:30 Handicap. This nine-year-old has 5 C&D wins from 23 starts, including February at 16/5 off 55, now at 58. His front-running suits the 6f Polytrack, with 14 AW wins total. Recent third and 9/2 odds with 5/1 support outpace rivals like Midnightattheoasis and Rebel Star.

Three wins at Wolverhampton and one at Lingfield to her name. Only beaten a nose at Wolverhampton last month. The trainer's form has dipped a bit recently but has still had two winners in the last two weeks and often springs a big priced winner. Jack Doughty's three pound claim looks significant.
Bred in the Purple won well on Polytrack twice last year. Didn't handle the heavy ground in GP1 Futurity last time, but this is a massive drop in class and should win on the snaff.
Upped in class here, but looks more than capable of running well after a five-length win over C&D last time out and looks the danger to the Gosden horse.
Likely found the ground too demanding when beaten by 9 lengths in the Royal Ledge Stakes last time. But was in good form prior to that.

Yaroogh looks a really nice type and nearly landed a Group 3 at Newbury last time, just racing a bit too keenly late on. That came off the back of a solid nursery win at Doncaster, so the talent’s definitely there. Still open to plenty of improvement and if he settles better, he’s got the class to be a big threat here.

Twice a winner as a two-year-old, he returned to action over a mile at Kempton and showed improved form to finish 2nd, keeping on nicely. He should stay further, but another bold show is on the cards.

Wolf Of Badenoch's career got off to a bright start in a Class 5 maiden and then ran a good 2nd in a Group 2 at Goodwood but somewhat disappointed in his last two races in the autumn. Could be worth an each-way on AW debut.
Just 3 runs to date and won at Kempton on the 2nd run back in January of this year, crucially over the same distance (1m) as tomorrow, and does not look like one to be underestimated.

Nammos can win Chelmsford’s 20:00 Handicap (7f). This three-year-old filly won her debut at Wolverhampton (6f) off 58, now at 60. Unexposed, her Siyouni pedigree suits the step to 7f, and her late-closing style fits Chelmsford’s Polytrack. Boughey’s 18% AW strike rate and 5/1 odds outshine exposed rivals like Poetic Jack.
Looked like the recent run at Lingfield would bring this one on. Won twice here over C&D last year and does look a bit of value in a competitive race.
Three times a course and distance winner, and last won last August off 76 at Lingfield. Huge chance back at his favourite track from a mark of just 70 and dropped into a 0-70 for the first time.
Kracking looks to be a sound each way bet in this. He has the speed, just needs to be held back a little longer based on his run at this venue a week ago.

Super Hit hasn’t been at his best since that win here in October, and was well beaten at Southwell last time, but the cheekpieces go on now and the yard’s in good nick. Back at a track he’s won at and off a workable mark, there’s a chance he could bounce back if the headgear change sparks him up.

I am picking Roach Power in this race despite its poor displays previously on the all-weather. Its record is three runs, and it has failed to place in any of them. It is down to a rating of 60 in this race, which is a career-low rating for it. I feel it can be competing for a place spot at this level. It is also wearing blinkers for the first time, and I am hoping that they can get a little improvement out of it.

Firmly at the bottom of the handicap mark in this field, but is a C&D winner and looks to be moving in the right direction after an encouraging effort LTO when 4th of 11 last month. It can cause an upset if improvements are made despite the mark staying the same.

3-year-old New Bay gelding is running in only his 2nd handicap today and had two previous runs here over 6 and 7 furlongs. He did not have the best of runs last time out and comes here again after a 187-day break. The sire suggests he should be suited by this course, and there has been money for today's run. Currently, he is the joint favorite.

Aim For The Bull didn’t land a blow last time at Wolverhampton but was a bit short of room late on and might have needed the run. Looks like he’ll be better over further, so this step up should suit, and the yard’s in great form with a strong record in all-weather handicaps here (194 runs, 22 wins, 11% strike rate, +85pts @ 44% ROI). Could take a step forward now conditions look more in his favour.
Went off favorite last time out at Southwell, but perhaps the surface did not suit nor the drop to six. Ran well prior over course and distance, and a repeat of that form would see this one win.

A weak-looking handicap where No Gain looks a decent punt at 15/2. He stepped up markedly on all previous form on his handicap debut at Wolves last month, and from the same mark again, can progress further to land this. The step down in trip looks a good move.

Daughter of Soldier's Call who was last seen at Wolverhampton 16 days ago where finishing 10th/11 however she is capable of shrugging off that latest effort and arrives here operating on a  basement mark of 47 now surely this daughter of Soldier's Call & Due Care ( Dam's sire Due Diligence ) is likely to better than a mark of 47 in very good time and can begin to make her presence felt the cheekpieces are applied for the first time here and they can have a positive effect this looks to be straightforward assignment for J Butler's inmate that looks pretty thin in nature and Due Respect can be whole different proposition this time out in a thin looking class 6 handicap has gate 1 here at Chelmsford that should put him in the perfect position with Jockey Lewis Edmunds taking the ride that being another positive factor . Respected .

Beaten into sixth on handicap at Southwell in February but finished only two lengths behind the winner. Raced wide throughout next time at Wolverhampton and likely better than she was able to show there. She's only had a handful of races and there could be more to come as she steps up in trip. Kieran O'Neill returns to the plate replacing seven pounds claiming apprentice, and she could outrun her big odds.

It remains to be seen how Handstands will perform on faster conditions at Aintree. He won his only point and won his first hurdle race on good going. This season, switching to fences, he fell in his first chase but has then been unbeaten in his last three races: two Grade 2 novice chases and last time a battling short-head win over Jango Baie at Sandown in a Grade 1 novice chase. He could win again.

Handstands is a warm favorite for this race and rightly so. Trends tend to favor those who ran at Cheltenham last time out. This lad fits the bill. He actually won at this meeting last season too, winning the Sefton Novices very comfortably, putting 5 lengths between himself and the runner-up, The Jukebox Man, at the finish, having traveled into the race like a very good thing. Admittedly, he needs to overcome a poor run in the Brown Advisory. He never seemed to enjoy himself on that occasion, so happy to draw a line through that run and give him another chance. He was 2/2 over fences prior to the last run, with the Grade 3 win being the pick of those efforts. He made all the running, jumped brilliantly, and was always in command. If he can repeat that run here, I think he can put it up to the favorite.

Caldwell Potter was hugely impressive at Cheltenham, making every yard. Jumping was superb. If allowed to bowl along in front again, could well be hard to pass. Hamdstand is the prime danger who looks to have been kept fresh for this.

Unlike most in this, it will definitely get the trip as the last 4 runs have all been at around this distance. One thing it probably won't get is the testing conditions that favor it. It has been 2nd on the last 2 runs at Navan and 23 days ago in the Brown Advisory, beaten 4L with 2 of today's rivals further behind.

The Changing Man does stay 3 miles and could go well if he has recovered from his exploits at Cheltenham where he was 2nd of 24, giving weight to the winner. He made all to win at Ascot and could do the same tomorrow.

I think in this field it looks the second most likely winner due to its potential, staying ability, enthusiasm, and its fantastic jumping ability. I've got a value price of 9/2 down, and Ladbrokes are offering a warm 9/2 on the horse. Looks, in my opinion, the best bet by a mile. Hanstands will be hard to beat, and Don't Rightly Know's trainer is currently out of form. But I still believe it has the 2nd best chance, and being the outsider of the field is just too big in my opinion. Should definitely be shorter on the off.

This horse was backed off the boards to land the ultra-competitive Martin Pipe race at the end of the Cheltenham Festival but flopped there. However, it is still unexposed and is clearly thought to be much better than that. I suspect early mistakes ruined his confidence, and maybe the 'lesser' jockey didn't give the horse the best ride on the day. So he's well worth another chance with Mark Walsh now in the saddle. For any horse to go off as short as 5/2 in the Martin Pipe on his fifth start, you'd have to say he's very highly thought of. Any horse is usually worth forgiving for one poor run, so the 13/2 is well worth taking.

Handicapper has left his mark untouched for the last run. To be fair, he stood little chance being ridden out wide throughout. Still, he travelled into contention before his run petered out. I still think he's well in off this type of mark based on his overall form. The trainer has saddled 2 of the last 3 winners of this race, so knows what it takes to win this event. His run behind Burdett Road in the Greatwood rates the standout piece of form. He was only beaten 1/2L by that horse. That form got boosted with Burdett Road finishing 2nd in the Champion Hurdle a few weeks back. If he repeats that form here, that would give him decent claims.

Another trainer who tends to target his runners at this race, having won this 3 times in the past. He ran a cracker in the Coral Cup last time out, sporting the first-time cheekpieces. He travelled into the race like the winner but was eventually run down late on by another of Willie Mullins' handicap good things in Jimmy Du Seuil. No disgrace there given that horse was massively chucked in off his handicap debut mark. The handicapper has reacted accordingly, shoving him up 4 lbs for that run, which means he must shoulder top weight in this race. His overall form would suggest he should be able to cope with the rise in the weights. He won well enough on his penultimate run at Newbury, again travelling into the race like a good thing, recording a nice easy win in the end. If he repeats that run and the Coral Cup run, he's probably the one to beat here if the weight concession isn't a problem for him.

The 6yo has 3 wins from 5 over hurdles. Tricky to weigh up the form from his last race, a 19L novice hurdle win. He’s best judged on his second start, on good ground, when a close second in an introductory hurdle race, splitting two smart rivals. His opening handicap mark looks handy. Strong jockey in the saddle.

WRECKLESS ERIC is likely a runner better suited by this flat track and the extra distance. The Imperial Cup at Sandown may be a decent season-long guide and this mildly progressive five year old representing the O'Neill trainer combination should be in the mix.

Steel Ally arrives in top form after a narrow second to Nemean Lion in a valuable Class 1, Grade 2 race at Fontwell, posting career-best figures in both performance and speed. That run came over a left-handed, sharp track similar to Aintree, making this a suitable test. Two starts back, he tackled a shorter 2-mile trip but lacked the speed to feature, while three runs ago, he secured a solid 3-length victory carrying 11st 11lb. His consistency, proven ability to improve with class, and strong showing in one of the most competitive races last time out make him a compelling contender here. Good luck!

Won 3 on the bounce on Good and Good to Soft. Followed that up with 4L 4th in a Listed contest and 4th in a G2. Has form behind Diva Luna in Listed and G2 Bumper, and that's worked out well. Harry Atkins takes off 7lb in a race the Skeltons have won 2 of the last 3.
I can see this being one of the best-backed horses on Friday. This is his time of year and he was a massive eye-catcher at Sandown when staying on from an impossible position.

Never discount these silks at Aintree. This one has some good course form after finishing 2nd to Jingo Baie in The Tolworth in December 2023. The tip has failed to trouble the judge in 3 runs this season from 15.5-16.5f and has never run over today's 20f trip, but I'll take a chance.
Expensive purchase Off The Jury is still a Maiden over hurdles, however, he has ran some cracking races in defeat. He could run very well at a stand-out 25/1 with bet365.

Blenkinsop was absent for 659 days after running in a three-mile Grade 1 novice hurdle at this Meeting in 2023 but looked to be coming back into form in his second race back at Uttoxeter last time when 3rd of 15 over this distance, beaten less than five lengths. If he comes on again for that run, he could go close at 50-1.

A typically tricky contest, and there are a few of interest that would have been primed for Cheltenham and may struggle to post their best efforts just three weeks later. Brentford Hope skipped Cheltenham and has been running in Graded company the last twice, first when behind Constitution Hill and then LTO last of four in the Kingwell. He was disappointing when last seen in handicap company, finishing down the field at Windsor, but that's a bit of a funny track, so I'm happy to forgive him that effort. He's undoubtedly well handicapped on the evidence of his Punchestown run last spring when finishing 2nd to Daddy Long Legs when giving that rival 8lbs, who has since won a Grade 3 and is now rated 151. I like spring festival form and big field handicap form, with Brentford Hope bringing both to the table, and a mark of 141 is 2lbs lower than his Punchestown run. He steps up in trip for the first time but seemed to see out 17f up the Cheltenham hill well enough in the Unibet Hurdle, and if the extra distance finds any improvement, he should be right in the mix.
Beacon Edge ran respectably when 7th in the Coral Cup at the Cheltenham Festival. Looks fairly handicapped, and the return to this easier track should suit.

Minella Missile is very well weighted on the best of his form. He has lost his form somewhat this season, but carries a low weight, and if anywhere near the level of ability when beating Captain Teague, he could make a mockery of these huge odds.

Not exactly a great price for this race, but I feel he's a solid choice given he ran a cracker in the Supreme Novices last time out. That race is usually a good prep for this one, with 9 of the last 12 winners of this running in the Supreme prior to coming here and taking this race. He's proven to be a useful horse this season. Form figures 1213. Winning his maiden on hurdling debut with any amount in hand. He managed to win the Grade 1 Paddy Power Novices on his penultimate run, beating stablemate Bleu De Vassy with any amount in hand. As mentioned above, he finished 3rd in the Supreme last time out. He ran very well, just couldn't match the finishing speed of the front two. He did stay on nicely enough, however. If he repeats that form here, he's the one to beat for me. He's a confident selection.
Totally Inexposed is improving at a rapid rate of knots this season. Served Cheltenham comes here fresh and could upset the hot pot.

Diva Luna won a bumper at this meeting last year, but her only hurdles win so far was in a maiden hurdle against geldings at Cheltenham on New Year's Day over two and a half miles. She finished 3rd of 23 last time at the Cheltenham Festival in a Grade 2 mares' novice hurdle over two miles one furlong. Could at least get a place, getting her seven-pound mares' allowance.

Arrives here off a mark of 137 and is improving every run. Won the last two, firstly at Ayr over 16f on soft in January, and then 34 days ago at Kelso, winning Grade 2 Novice Hurdle on good to soft over 18f with the fancied W. Mullins' favourite 2.5L behind in 2nd. Drops back 2f in trip today shouldn't be a problem.
This horse has done nothing but improve this season. He beat 2 decent performers last time out at Newbury and looks a huge each way price.

Loves courses starting with the letter A, namely Ascot and here at Aintree, where he's undefeated in 4 runs. He comes back here to defend his crown he won last year, facing only 3 opponents: 1. Protektorat, who he beat last year; another, El Fabiola, who's better at a shorter distance despite being 1 lb higher in rating; and lastly, Matata, whose 2 runs here have seen 10th out of 10 runners and 6th out of 12. Jonbon will be a skinny price, but the smaller field and hopefully better start than his Cheltenham run, where he ran on well to finish 2nd, was still disappointing. He should avenge that result.

El Fabiolo has met Jonbon three times, with Jonbon holding on in a photo finish over hurdles here in 2022. At the Cheltenham Festival the following year, El Fabiolo won the Arkle from Jonbon by over five lengths despite a mistake at the last. Since making it seven wins in a row in the Grade 1 Dublin Chase in February 2024, Fabiolo's jumping has been problematic, and he lost out to Jonbon at Sandown through mistakes in 2024. The Mildmay Course at Aintree is a less demanding jumping test, and if El Fabiolo gets round with only one minor mistake, he could have too much pace for Jonbon at the finish.

Sits just 1 lb above the mark he ran off when finishing a solid 2nd in this race last season. He ran a cracker in this last season. Enjoyed every minute of this demanding course. Looked to have them all at it jumping the final fence before he was run down late on by Arizona Cardinal. Beaten just 1L. His campaign has been geared around a repeat run in this race. Finishing out the back of the tele on a number of occasions. I felt his most recent run showed some promise, however. Not beaten all that far in 5th place. Paul Townsend jumps off and rides Blue Lord this time, having ridden him in this event last year. To be fair, I'd rather side with the one we know handles this demanding track rather than back an unknown quantity. He's got solid claims of going one better this time around with JJ Slevin in the saddle.

BLUE LORD got within two and a half lengths of Corbetts Cross last time out on level weights, which is some going. That run perhaps flatters the selection a little as Corbetts Cross was surely only using that as a prep for the Cheltenham Gold Cup, but nevertheless, it reads well going back into handicap company. I think the selection ought to make the frame if getting a clear passage, and I wouldn't be totally surprised if he won this a shade cosily. Paul Townend back onboard is another big plus.

Bad comes into this race in outstanding form, having won his last two starts while showing progressive improvement in class, weight carried, speed figures, and overall performance. Each run has demonstrated a clear upward trajectory, proving he can handle stronger competition. His latest victory at Kempton, a sharp track similar to Aintree, was impressive. He showed a good cruising speed, traveled strongly throughout, and found plenty when asked, suggesting he still has more to offer. Despite going up in weight, he carries 6lbs less than in that win. Given his consistency, proven ability to step up, and strong positioning in my ratings, the 16/1 price represents value. He looks primed for another big run. Good luck!

EXCELLO is interesting as a Nicky Henderson trained chaser who looks well treated at the base of this handicap chase. The cheek pieces are fitted and this six year old boasts some early career winning form over fences in France which can serve him well. Possibly a plan by connections and no real surprise if he were punted.

This one has winning form here and at Cheltenham and was only beaten 7L when 2nd in the Glenfarclas Cross Country at Cheltenham last time for this team. Gina Andrews is more than able to take this type of race, and this one goes well for her. So he is the pick to take this race.

Marble Sands is usually ridden by a conditional, but the stable jockey is on board now for the first time since being on for the horse's last win. That looks significant since the horse has been given a chance by the handicapper here. He races off 143 and won off 146 for that last win for this jockey, which was over virtually the same trip and ground as he gets here today. The stable couldn't be any hotter either, with 6 of their last 8 runners winning, which is an incredible purple patch for them.

This one has run at the Cheltenham Festival twice, falling in 2024 and was well beaten 15/20 in the Grand Annual this year. It is not often that horses who run well at Cheltenham can repeat the feat here, so a chance is taken that this one will show his best form on his first visit here. A small E/W at 22/1 would be a value bet.

Not really a strong candidate for win purposes, admittedly. But boasts decent enough each-way claims in this wide-open affair. She loves this track. She also ran a cracker in this event back in 2023. A shade unlucky in defeat. She was hampered by a loose horse, causing her to lose vital momentum at a crucial stage of the race. She was beaten just over 1L by the winner back in 2nd place. The ground is key to her. She prefers faster going, but to be fair, she can go on softer ground also. Her best form has come on quicker going, however. She's vulnerable for win purposes, admittedly. But is a nice enough price to chance each-way in the hope she can hit the frame with 6 places up for grabs with ground and track to suit.

9-year-old gelding who has recorded 6 top 3 finishes, including 4 victories from 14 starts over fences. Although his overall record is rather hit and miss, he can be easily forgiven his latest defeat as he whipped around at the start of the race at Cheltenham. With most of his best form having been achieved on quickish ground, this prominent racer has each-way claims on his first attempt over the Grand National fences.

The 8yo has a progressive profile. Five runs this campaign, below par in two soft ground races but solid efforts in three good ground races. He lost by a nk in a Grade 2 on his return during Nov, similar trip and going as this handicap - the form boosted by the winner since. He was a Grade 2 winner during Dec. He was beaten a length last month in an £8K handicap, which looked like a fitness run and he’s in good shape. Every chance off his current handicap mark.
Eldorado Allen ran well for a long way in last year's Grand National before weakening late on. He is now lower in the weights, and the drop in distance looks ideal.

Shows some good form figures against other horses in this race. 1 win and 2 places from 7 runs in this class, 3 wins and 3 places from 17 chases. The going will suit today and each way chance at 50/1.

Mister Meggit runs here fresh from comfortably winning his only hurdle race here over two and a half miles back in November. He can also erase the disappointment of being a beaten favourite here in the bumper at this meeting where he stumbled three furlongs out and could not recover.

Steps up in trip for the first time under rules, which is a wise idea given his P2P form. He's proven to be a solid horse over hurdles, winning 2 of his 3 runs. He won in a hack canter on hurdling debut. Admittedly, it wasn't a deep race, but he was most impressive. He bumped into the high-class The New Lion next time out, beaten 3L by the winner. No disgrace there given that horse went on to Turners at the festival. He's now 4/4 under rules. He got himself back into the winner's enclosure last time out, finding plenty for pressure to land a listed race, beating No Questions Asked by 1/2L. He showed great battling qualities to get back up and deny the runner-up. That last run hinted at a step up in trip being what he needs. He looks a stayer, all stamina. This is a step up on anything he's done to date, but he looks the type to progress now stepped up in distance.

The 6yo has 2 wins from 2 over hurdles, still unexposed. He was a Grade 2 winner over this 3m trip last time out, never in trouble when winning by 5L and the form looks decent. Will be fresh after a 7 week break and can take another step forward.

6yo mare who finished third on her debut over hurdles, but has since won twice, including a Grade 3 event for mares at Limerick. She was awarded a career-best RPR of 133 for that effort, which suggests that she may be capable of going close in this race, with further improvement likely.

WESTERN KNIGHT ran well in Grade 2 company on his penultimate start and he remains unexposed in the staying division with an abundance of potential. He gets to take his chance with the yard in decent form and last raced around ten weeks ago there has to be a chance he has been saved for this renewal.

2 wins and 2 places from 5 jumps races is a pretty good record, albeit not at this class. But it has superior form over Jupiter Des Mottes, also in this race, and will perform at this going. Each way chance at big odds.

Won a bumper when with N. Richards, then changed yards and has had 2 runs on soft in class 4 hurdles. Winning at Newcastle over 20.5f, then 27 days ago was 2nd at Ayr again over 20.5f on soft. Still very unexposed and open to lots more improvement.

Put up a cracking performance 34 days ago when 2nd of 18 in a hot looking Kelso class 2. That was off a career high mark and with a 5lb claim today my selection can run off effectively a 2lb lower mark. That must bring him into the calculations especially on a flat galloping track like Aintree and with the yard in fine form he looks overpriced.

Five hurdle runs for the 6yo, two narrow defeats followed by three wins in a row. He’s not been troubled when winning his novice hurdle races. His opening handicap mark could be lenient and he’s now helped by a very good apprentice who takes a useful 7lb off his back.

7-year-old gelding who has never finished worse than fourth in any of his 9 starts in NH flat races and over hurdles. He recorded his third victory over hurdles when successful at Stratford last time out and remains open to further improvement. Hopefully, he can reward each-way support.
This one won under this jockey off 121 last time and now goes up 3lb to only 1lb higher than his last win. This jockey is worth his 5lb claim, and this one has every chance to follow up at 18/1.

8/11 aged 5-7. 1/11 fav, 1/11 top 3 in the betting. 9/12 carried 11st2 or less, 8/11 rated 129+. G. Elliot won this in 2019. Lightly raced and bought off the flat in France. Struggled in his first 3 runs but put in a nice performance last time out. 4L win on soft going away and could have won much further. Kennedy said post-race he'd improve for better ground and that it was very testing, and he did well to get through it. Likely improvement to come and overpriced at 20s. May just lack a bit of experience.

Country Park won his only point but frustratingly has remained a maiden under rules so far in two bumpers and seven hurdle races. Although he has shown promise in his last six races with three 2nd places, a 3rd, and a 4th of 11 last time. In his other race, he looked to be going best, closing behind the leaders when falling two out at Ascot. Benjamin Macey takes off seven pounds to mitigate him being a pound out of the handicap.

Has some very smart form to his name. Although it was a poor performance at Sandown, at no stage was he traveling a repeat of Welsh Hurdle run. The runner-up effort behind Sir Gino in Fighting Fifth could see this Sam Thomas runner outrun odds of 25/1.

Over the course of the last 6 runs, has 2 wins at Kelso on good to soft over 16f and Wetherby on good over 16f, both in class 3 races. Has been placed on 2 other occasions at Kelso over 16f on soft, and then 34 days ago at Kelso once again over 16f on good to soft but up into a class 2 race. Only a 6-year-old and runs off a mark of 123 with a claimer taking 7 lb off, still lots of improvement to come.
Catch Him Derry runs this distance well on good to soft and has to overcome an eight-pound rise for his last two races: a win at Exeter and a 3rd of 24 at the Cheltenham Festival.

This horse is a real potential improver that is less exposed than virtually all of these and looks to have been put away with this race in mind. The close up third at Newbury behind The New Lion has had the form franked innumerable times and that really does look a cracking effort in the context of this race. The trainer is trying a tongue tie now to squeeze out any further improvement and there could well be an awful lot more to come from this 6yo.

8yo gelding who has won twice from 6 starts over hurdles. He recorded a career best RPR of 142 when winning a handicap hurdle at Thurles on his latest start. He will probably need to improve on that effort to overcome his new OR of 140, but he clearly stays well and he should not be inconvenienced by the underfoot conditions.

This race tends to go to horses towards the top end of the market historically. But I want to take a chance on this mare. She's on a decent mark and has a very good 3lbs claiming jockey booked to ride. She's got it all to do in terms of bucking trends. Even the ground would be an issue, but she's a huge price. I just can't let her go unbacked given her overall form. She finished a decent 5th in the Stayers' Hurdle over in Ireland, beaten just 11L by the winner Teahupoo. She had the likes of Asterion Furlonge, Home By The Lee, and Buddy One in front of her. No disgrace there given the caliber of opposition. She ran well last time out. Looked to hold a decent chance before being outpaced over a sharp enough trip, finishing in 5th place, beaten 10L or so. She's unexposed over this distance, so I think she's got an each-way squeak if handling the faster ground.
Lulamba goes up in distance and takes on his elders, but this close 2nd in the Triumph Hurdle should win with his age allowance of ten pounds.

I was shocked that Horaces Pearl did not run in the Supreme as it could have been Fergal's first Cheltenham Festival winner. This horse won at the Aintree Festival last year, and the longer distance will suit. Will be fresh from not running at Cheltenham. My tip of the week. Hoping the horse will prove how good he is. Future World Hurdle horse for next year.

CASTLE CARROCK does give the impression he is a big price having caught the eye in Grade 2 novice hurdle company latest. He represents a powerful shrewd British dual-purpose yard and so in a race where an each-way play could be the way to go he appeals.

IMPERIAL SAINT has a strong French sire and is clearly a better horse turning left-handed. He is also fully effective at this flat track and still relatively unexposed especially over this more extreme distance he rates a solid candidate for this renewal.

Docpickedme comes here fresh following a break of 70 days since winning at Doncaster and he previously just lost out to bottom weight Charlie Uberalles also at Doncaster. Charlie Maggs rode him last time and his allowance takes his weight down to ten stone and Aintree suits frontrunners like Docpickedme.

Sits on a nice mark at present. Having also skipped the festival to come here. Having just his 2nd handicap run. He's had just 3 runs this season. All 3 runs over fences. On reappearance he made a mockery of his handicap mark (132). Beating Westerninthepark comfortably. He then ran another solid race behind recent Cheltenham Festival winner Haiti Couleurs. Beaten just 3L by the winner back in 3rd place. A solid run trying to give 9lbs in weight to the winner. He switched yards and made his debut for them back in February. He ran no race at all. A well beaten 3rd behind the Changing Man in a Grade 2. I'm willing to just write off that run and give him another chance here. If he can show that form behind Haiti Couleurs here this time. He's got decent claims off this type of mark.

8yo gelding who has posted 5 top 3 finishes, but only 1 victory from 12 starts over fences. He has recorded his top 3 RPRs over fences in his last 3 starts and remains realistically treated off his current OR of 135, compared with his best RPR of 140.

Not a solid proposition by any means. He's now 11 years old also and missed 2 years of racing due to injury. So it remains to be seen how much ability he has left intact. Since joining this stable, he's run in 2 ultra-competitive handicaps at Cheltenham. He ran okay after a long break on reappearance and stable debut back in January, finishing in 5th place off a 4 lbs higher mark than this. He ran like he desperately needed that run. He ran a belter in the Ultima last time out. Made stealthy progress, running on into 4th place, beaten 15 lengths by the winner. The winner did win that race by 11 lengths, so it's not as bad a run as it sounds. He's been dropped another 1 lb for that effort. He won this race back in 2021 off a 10 lbs higher mark. I think he can run into a place at least if repeating the last effort.
